aria: Animated recap of the Spurs' 124 to 112 home win over the Clippers: Julian Champagnie's 3-pointer off a Stephon Castle steal with 7:55 left that made it 105 to 97, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Victor Wembanyama's 32 points and 11 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Spurs won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Spurs' 124–112 home win over the LA Clippers on Nov 19, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked against the SI box score and scoring play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News), USA Today (via Yahoo Sports) and The Sporting Tribune (via Yahoo Sports). All 124 San Antonio points and all 112 Clippers points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (24–33–35–32 to 21–33–34–24) add up to both totals: 57–54 San Antonio at the half and 92–88 after three (SI; The Sporting Tribune; the CBS Sports gametracker shows the same first three quarters). Team totals (points in the paint 54–36, assists 37–24, steals 15–11, free throws 21 of 23 to 15 of 17, threes 11 of 31 to 17 of 42) are from the box score; the paint and three-point numbers match the written stories. The biggest leads, 14 for San Antonio and 6 for the Clippers, are from the box score and the SI play-by-play. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Thursday's games.

Victor Wembanyama had 32 points and 11 rebounds on 13 of 26 shooting, his seventh 30-point game of the season, and Stephon Castle had 21 points and 12 assists (AP). San Antonio had lost 105–93 to Detroit on Tuesday, ending a 12-game winning streak (AP; USA Today). Castle's three made it 38–28, the Spurs' first double-digit lead, four minutes into the second quarter (AP; The Sporting Tribune). Brook Lopez and Max Strus answered the play of the game with back-to-back threes, and Lopez's fifth three with 2:25 left cut it to eight (The Sporting Tribune; SI). The Spurs played without Dylan Harper (hip) (AP; USA Today). San Antonio hosts New Orleans on Saturday, Nov 21 at 8:00 PM ET (AP; SI schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Julian Champagnie's 3-pointer with 7:55 left that made it 105–97 (SI play-by-play; AP and The Sporting Tribune put it at about eight minutes left). Castle stole the ball and found Champagnie for the three (AP; The Sporting Tribune; the SI play-by-play lists Castle's assist), so the board shows Spurs +5 to +8 (102–97 to 105–97). It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the spot and the defender are not drawn to exact positions. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Julian Champagnie's listed 6-foot-7 and 217 pounds with No. 30 (Wikipedia); no wingspan from a named measurement was found, so his arms use the default length. He is drawn in San Antonio's home kit with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
